title: HDAC1 activity transduces remote voltage change into tumor suppression

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HDAC1 activity transduces remote voltage change into tumor suppression

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Histone deacetylase 1 activity is the main transduction step by which hyperpolarization of distant cells suppresses tumorigenesis in Xenopus laevis, since expressing a dominant-negative HDAC1 at a site remote from KRASG12D-expressing cells raises the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 36%.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: introducing DN-HDAC1 non-locally to the site of KRASG12D increased ITLS formation incidence by 35.6% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 5C), suggesting a role for histone deacetylase 1 activity controlling cell behavior at a distance.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “RESULTS › Changes in Vmem”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D and dominant-negative HDAC1 mRNA in separate blastomeres under hyperpolarizing high-chloride conditions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing intervention results directly test whether HDAC1 activity modifies suppression. They do not fully distinguish pathway transduction from independent HDAC effects or establish that HDAC1 is the main mediator.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare KRAS tumor incidence during remote hyperpolarization with and without dominant-negative HDAC1 and against disruptions of alternative transduction pathways. Rescue of incidence specifically by HDAC1 disruption would support its role.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The intervention establishes involvement more readily than 'main transduction step'.

Dominant-negative HDAC1 may alter tumorigenesis independently.

Raw contingency data are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The remote dominant-negative HDAC1 contrast is numerically published and can be checked for direction and reported significance. Calling HDAC1 the main transduction step goes beyond that one intervention. Acetylation readouts that would tie the incidence change to HDAC1 activity are not in a public dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Under hyperpolarizing high-chloride conditions, express dominant-negative HDAC1 remote from KRASG12D and compare tumor-like-structure incidence with a control construct. An increase near the reported 36% would support an HDAC1 step; no increase, or an increase with HDAC1 activity intact, would refute HDAC1 as the necessary transducer.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Acetylation and remote voltage were not deposited animal by animal.

A single dominant-negative construct does not show that HDAC1 is the main transducer rather than one contributing factor.
